name: ChatGPT
tagline: General-purpose AI assistant for writing, learning and analysis.
best_for: Everyday questions, drafting and study help
description:
ChatGPT is a conversational assistant from OpenAI. You type a question or instruction and it replies in plain language, which makes it useful for explaining ideas, drafting emails, brainstorming, summarising text and practising a new subject.

Its biggest strength is flexibility: the same chat can help you outline an essay, check a spreadsheet formula and rehearse an interview. Paid plans typically add access to stronger models and extra features such as file uploads and image tools, but what is included changes over time, so check the official plans page. Like every AI assistant it can sound confident while being wrong, so treat answers as a first draft and verify facts, numbers and quotes before using them in schoolwork or at work.
use_steps: Open the website or app and sign in.
Describe the task, your level and the format you want.
Ask follow-up questions, then verify important facts elsewhere.
pros: Handles many kinds of tasks in one place

name: Claude
tagline: AI assistant known for long documents and careful writing.
best_for: Reading long texts and structured writing
description:
Claude is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. People often choose it for working with long documents and for careful, readable writing. You can paste or upload a report, ask for a summary, then ask follow-up questions about specific sections.

It is a good fit for editing drafts, explaining dense material in simpler words and thinking through a problem step by step. As with other assistants, it can make mistakes, so check names, dates and calculations yourself. Features, limits and plans change regularly; the official site shows what your account includes. For sensitive documents, read the privacy information before uploading anything.
use_steps: Sign in on the website or app.
Paste text or attach a document and say what you need.
Refine with follow-up questions and check key facts.
cons: Can still be wrong on facts

name: Google Gemini
tagline: Google’s AI assistant connected to Google apps.
best_for: People who live in Google Workspace
description:
Gemini is Google's AI assistant. Its main appeal is the link with Google services: depending on your account and settings it can work with things like Gmail, Docs, Drive and Search, so you can ask it to summarise a long email thread or help draft a document without copying text between apps.

It can also take images as input, which helps when you want a photo of a diagram or a worksheet explained. If you already live in a Google account, it is a low-friction place to start. Availability of features varies by country, age and account type, and Google changes plans often, so confirm what you get on the official page. Always double-check factual answers.
use_steps: Open the Gemini site or app with a Google account.
Ask a question or attach a file or image.
Use the share or export options to move results into Docs.
cons: Features depend on account and region

name: Microsoft Copilot
tagline: AI assistant built into Microsoft products and the web.
description:
Microsoft Copilot is an assistant that appears on the web, in Windows and inside Microsoft 365 apps such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. In those apps it can draft text, summarise long emails, suggest formulas and build a first-draft slide deck from a document.

It is most useful if your school or workplace already uses Microsoft 365, because it can work with the files you have access to. Which features you see depends on your licence and organisation settings, and some are paid add-ons, so check with your administrator or the official page. As with all AI output, review it before sending or submitting.
use_steps: Open Copilot on the web or inside a Microsoft app.
Describe what you want, or select a document to work on.
Review the result and edit it before sharing.
pros: Helps with documents, email and slides
cons: Best features need a paid licence

name: Perplexity
tagline: AI answer engine that cites its sources.
best_for: Quick research with links to check
description:
Perplexity works like a search engine that writes a short answer and shows numbered sources next to it. That makes it handy for quick research, because you can click through to the original pages and check what was actually said.

It is strong for questions where you want recent information and links, and weaker when you need deep reasoning about your own documents. Remember that a cited answer is not automatically correct: read the sources, especially for health, legal or money topics. Plans and limits change, so look at the official page for what the free and paid versions include.
use_steps: Open the site and type your question.
Read the answer and open two or three of the cited sources.
Use follow-up questions to narrow the topic.

name: Grok
tagline: AI assistant from xAI with live social data.
description:
Grok is the AI assistant from xAI. It is available on the Grok website and apps and is closely tied to the X platform, which means it can talk about what people are discussing there in real time.

That can be useful for following fast-moving topics, but social posts are noisy and often wrong, so treat anything it says about breaking news carefully and confirm with trusted outlets. Like other assistants it can also help with writing, code and general questions. Access levels and prices have changed several times; check the official site for what is free and what needs a subscription today.
use_steps: Open Grok on the web or in the app.
Ask a question or request a draft.
Check time-sensitive claims against reliable news sources.

name: DeepSeek
tagline: Open-weights AI assistant focused on reasoning and coding.
description:
DeepSeek is an AI assistant and model family known for strong reasoning and coding results at low cost. You can chat with it on its website and app, and some of its models are published as open weights, which lets developers run them on their own systems.

It is popular with students and programmers who want step-by-step solutions to maths and code problems. Because the hosted service is operated by a company outside many users' own country, read its privacy policy and avoid entering personal or confidential information. Check the official site for current models and limits.
use_steps: Open the DeepSeek site or app.
Paste a problem and ask for step-by-step reasoning.
Verify the final answer by running the code or checking the maths.

name: Grammarly
tagline: Grammar, tone and clarity checker.
description:
Grammarly checks writing as you type and suggests fixes for spelling, grammar, punctuation and clarity. It works in browsers, desktop apps and many text boxes, so you can use it in email, documents and social posts.

Beyond corrections, it can suggest changes in tone and conciseness, and newer versions include generative writing features. It is a safe way to learn from your mistakes if you read each suggestion rather than clicking accept on all of them. Because it reads what you type, check the privacy settings before using it with confidential text. Plans and features change, so see the official pricing page.
use_steps: Install the browser extension or desktop app.
Write as usual and review the underlined suggestions.
Accept only the changes that keep your meaning.

name: QuillBot
tagline: Paraphrasing, summarising and grammar tools.
description:
QuillBot offers a set of writing tools, mainly a paraphraser, a summariser, a grammar checker and a citation helper. The paraphraser rewrites a sentence in different words and lets you choose how much to change.

Students use it to simplify heavy text or to find a clearer way to say something. Be careful with academic work: rewording someone else's text without credit is still plagiarism, and many schools have rules about AI assistance. Use it to improve your own writing, not to hide copied material. Check the official site for current limits and plans.
use_steps: Open the paraphraser or summariser.
Paste your own text and pick a mode.
Compare with the original and edit by hand.
pros: Several writing tools in one place

name: Notion AI
tagline: AI features inside the Notion workspace.
best_for: Notes and project docs in Notion
description:
Notion AI adds writing and organising help inside the Notion workspace where many people keep notes, tasks and wikis. It can summarise a page, pull out action items, rewrite a paragraph and answer questions about the content you store there.

Its value comes from being where your notes already live: you do not need to copy text into another tool. If you do not use Notion, it offers little. Notion has a free plan, but the AI features depend on your plan and can change, so check the official pricing page before you rely on them. Review any generated summary against the original notes.
use_steps: Open a Notion page and invoke the AI menu.
Choose summarise, action items or write.
Edit the result and keep the original text nearby.
pros: Good for meeting notes and wikis
cons: Only useful if you use Notion

name: Otter.ai
tagline: Meeting transcription and summaries.
description:
Otter records and transcribes meetings, lectures and interviews, then produces searchable notes and a short summary. It can join online meetings, and there is also a phone app for recording in person.

It saves time when you want to focus on the conversation instead of typing. Accuracy depends on audio quality and accents, so skim the transcript before quoting anyone. Always tell participants when you record and follow your school's or employer's rules and local laws. Free and paid limits change, so confirm on the official page.
use_steps: Connect your calendar or open the app.
Start recording or add the bot to a meeting.
Review the summary and fix names or terms.

name: Fireflies.ai
tagline: AI meeting recorder and note taker.
best_for: Teams that meet on video calls
description:
Fireflies is an AI note taker that joins video calls, records them with permission and creates a transcript, summary and list of action items. It connects with common meeting platforms and can send notes to other tools.

Teams like it because everyone can search past meetings by keyword. Make sure all participants know the meeting is being recorded and check your organisation's rules before using it with confidential topics. Transcripts are rarely perfect, so review key decisions. Plans and limits change, so see the official site for the current free and paid options.
use_steps: Connect your calendar and meeting app.
Let the bot join and record with consent.
Review the summary and share action items.

name: Zapier
tagline: Connects apps and automates workflows.
description:
Zapier connects different web apps so they can pass information to each other without code. You build a workflow, called a Zap, from a trigger (for example, a new form response) and one or more actions (add a row to a sheet, send an email, post a message).

It is useful for small teams and individuals who repeat the same copy-and-paste tasks. Start with one simple automation and test it before relying on it, because a wrong setting can send messages to the wrong people. Task limits and plans change, so check the official pricing page.
use_steps: Create an account and choose a trigger app.
Pick the action you want to happen automatically.
Test the Zap with sample data before turning it on.

name: Canva
tagline: Design tool with AI image and writing features.
description:
Canva is a browser-based design tool with templates for presentations, posters, social posts, resumes and videos. You drag elements onto a page, change colours and fonts, and export the result as an image or PDF.

It also includes AI helpers for things like generating images or rewriting text. It is a good starting point for people without design training because templates handle layout. Some templates, photos and features are limited to paid plans, and licence rules apply to stock content, so check the official terms before using designs commercially.
use_steps: Choose a template for your format.
Replace the text and images with your own.
Download as PDF or PNG.
cons: Many assets need a paid plan

name: Gamma
tagline: AI-assisted presentations and documents.
description:
Gamma generates a presentation, document or simple web page from a prompt or an outline. You describe the topic, pick a style, and it builds slides you can edit with a card-based editor.

It is useful for getting past the blank page quickly. Treat the first version as a draft: check every claim, replace generic text with your own examples and remove slides that do not support your point. Free access and credits change, so look at the official page for the current limits.
use_steps: Enter a topic or paste an outline.
Choose a theme and generate.
Edit each card and export or share.

name: Beautiful.ai
tagline: Presentation software with smart layouts.
description:
Beautiful.ai is presentation software that keeps slides tidy automatically. When you add or move content, its smart templates adjust spacing and alignment, so you spend less time fixing layout.

It also includes AI features to draft slides. It suits business presentations where consistency matters. It is a paid product with a free trial that has changed over time, so confirm current terms before you start, and export a backup of your deck.
use_steps: Start from a template or generate a draft.
Add your own content in the smart slides.
Present online or export.

name: Figma
tagline: Collaborative interface design tool.
description:
Figma is a collaborative design tool that runs in the browser. Designers use it to create app screens, website layouts, icons and prototypes, and teammates can comment or edit in the same file at the same time.

It has a learning curve compared with simple graphic tools, but it is the standard for interface design and has a large community of free templates. Students can often find education plans. Features and limits on free plans change, so check the official site.
use_steps: Create a free account and open a new design file.
Draw frames and add components.
Share a link for feedback and use prototype mode to test flows.

name: Midjourney
tagline: AI image generator known for artistic output.
description:
Midjourney generates images from text prompts and is known for a distinctive artistic look. It is used for concept art, mood boards, book covers and stylised illustrations.

You describe the image, review variations and refine by adjusting the prompt or choosing options. Results are strong on style but can struggle with accurate text and anatomy. Check the terms about commercial use and whether your images are public by default. It is a paid service, so see the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Sign in and open the creation interface.
Write a prompt describing subject, style and lighting.
Pick a variation and refine the prompt.

name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Adobe’s generative AI for images and effects.
description:
Adobe Firefly is Adobe's family of generative AI tools for creating images, extending photos and applying text effects. Adobe says its models are trained on licensed and public-domain content, which matters to people who worry about copyright.

Firefly also connects with Photoshop and Illustrator, so you can fill or expand an image inside the apps you already use. Usage is measured in credits, and free credits and paid plans change, so check the official page. Always review generated images for errors.
use_steps: Open Firefly on the web or in an Adobe app.
Describe the image or select an area to edit.
Download or continue editing in Photoshop.

name: Leonardo AI
tagline: AI image generation with style controls.
description:
Leonardo AI is an image generation platform popular with game artists and designers. It offers different models and style presets, plus tools for refining images, creating variations and training small custom styles.

It is a good choice when you want more control than a single prompt box gives you. Free tokens and plan details change, so check the official site. Review licence terms before commercial use and double-check generated images for flaws.
use_steps: Create an account and choose a model.
Write a prompt and select a style preset.
Refine with variations or editing tools.

name: Ideogram
tagline: AI image generator good at text in images.
description:
Ideogram is an AI image generator that is better than many tools at putting readable text into pictures, such as poster titles, logos and signs.

You write a prompt, choose a style and aspect ratio, and compare results. Text can still contain errors, so zoom in and proofread before publishing. Free and paid options change, so check the official site and read the terms on commercial use.
use_steps: Open the site and write your prompt, including the exact text.
Choose a style and ratio.
Generate and proofread the lettering.

name: Remove.bg
tagline: Removes image backgrounds automatically.
description:
Remove.bg removes the background from a photo automatically in seconds. Upload an image of a person, product or object and download a version with a transparent background.

It is handy for ID photos, product pictures for online shops and design projects. Complex hair or glass edges may need touch-ups. Free downloads are usually smaller than paid high-resolution ones, and pricing changes, so check the official site.
use_steps: Upload your photo.
Wait for the automatic cut-out.
Download the transparent PNG or add a new background.

name: Upscayl
tagline: Free open-source AI image upscaler.
description:
Upscayl is a free, open-source desktop app that enlarges low-resolution images using AI models running on your own computer. Because it runs locally, your pictures are not uploaded to a server.

It works best on clean images and can add artefacts to very poor ones. A computer with a decent graphics card makes it faster. Download it only from the official project page and check the licence and release notes.
use_steps: Download from the official page and install.
Select an image and choose a model and scale.
Upscale and compare with the original.
cons: Not magic on very blurry images

name: Runway
tagline: AI video generation and editing suite.
description:
Runway is a creative suite for AI video. You can generate short clips from text or images, remove backgrounds from video, and use editing tools that normally take hours.

It is used by filmmakers, marketers and students experimenting with new ideas. Generated clips are short and may show visual glitches, so plan to edit and combine them. Usage is based on credits and plans change, so check the official site and the rules about commercial use.
use_steps: Create an account and choose a generation tool.
Describe the scene or upload a start image.
Download the clip and edit it in your video editor.

name: Pika
tagline: Text and image to video generator.
description:
Pika turns text prompts or images into short video clips and offers effects such as adding or transforming objects in a scene. It is popular with social media creators who want eye-catching short clips quickly.

Expect short outputs and occasional visual oddities. Free access, credits and commercial-use rules have changed, so check the official page before using clips in a business. Always review results for artefacts before posting.
use_steps: Sign in and pick text-to-video or image-to-video.
Describe the motion you want.
Download and trim in an editor.

name: CapCut
tagline: Video editor with auto-captions and AI tools.
description:
CapCut is a video editor for phone, desktop and browser that is especially popular for short-form videos. It includes templates, automatic captions, background removal and many effects.

It suits beginners who want to make a polished clip quickly. Some effects and exports are limited to the paid version, and the app's terms and availability can vary by country, so check the official site. Review auto captions for mistakes before posting.
use_steps: Import clips into a new project.
Trim, add captions and effects.
Export in the size your platform needs.

name: Descript
tagline: Edit video and audio by editing text.
description:
Descript lets you edit audio and video by editing a transcript. Delete a word from the text and it disappears from the recording, which makes cutting filler words and mistakes very quick.

It is popular for podcasts, interviews and talking-head videos. It also offers features such as screen recording and AI voice tools. Transcription is not perfect, so check names. Plans and limits change; see the official site.
use_steps: Import a recording and let it transcribe.
Edit the text to cut or reorder sections.
Export audio or video.

name: ElevenLabs
tagline: Realistic AI voice generation.
description:
ElevenLabs creates natural-sounding AI voices from text and can also clone a voice when you have the right to do so. It is used for narration, audiobooks, videos and accessibility.

Use only voices you have permission to copy and follow the service's rules on consent. Listen to the whole result for mispronunciations. Free allowances and paid plans change, so check the official site and licence terms for commercial use.
use_steps: Paste your script and choose a voice.
Adjust speed and stability settings.
Generate, listen fully and download.

name: Whisper (OpenAI)
tagline: Open-source speech recognition model.
description:
Whisper is an open-source speech recognition model released by OpenAI. It turns spoken audio into text in many languages and can also translate speech to English.

Because the code is available, developers can run it on their own computers so audio stays private. It is a command-line or code-based tool, so it is better suited to people comfortable with Python than to beginners, though many apps are built on top of it. Accuracy depends on audio quality.
use_steps: Install it following the project instructions.
Run it on an audio file with your chosen model size.
Proofread the transcript.

name: Audacity
tagline: Free open-source audio editor.
description:
Audacity is a free, open-source audio editor for Windows, macOS and Linux. You can record, cut, merge and clean up audio, remove background noise and apply effects.

It is a classic choice for podcasts and voice-overs, though its interface looks dated. Download it only from the official site to avoid fake installers. It does not use AI to edit for you, but it is reliable and has no cost.
use_steps: Download from the official site and install.
Record or import audio.
Apply noise reduction and export as MP3 or WAV.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: AI pair programmer inside your editor.
description:
GitHub Copilot suggests code as you type inside editors such as VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. It can complete a line, write a function from a comment and answer questions about your code in a chat panel.

It speeds up routine work but can propose incorrect or insecure code, so read and test everything. It is a paid product with some education access and free options that have varied, so check the official page for what applies to you.
use_steps: Install the extension in your editor and sign in.
Write a comment describing the function you want.
Review, test and edit the suggestion.

name: Cursor
tagline: AI-first code editor.
best_for: Working across a codebase with AI
description:
Cursor is a code editor built around AI. It looks like VS Code but adds chat and editing features that can read your project, suggest changes across several files and explain unfamiliar code.

It is helpful for learning a codebase and for repetitive edits. Review every change it proposes and use version control so you can undo mistakes. It offers a free tier with limits and paid plans; the details change often, so check the official pricing page.
use_steps: Download and open your project folder.
Ask the chat to explain or change a file.
Review the diff before accepting.

name: Replit
tagline: Browser-based coding environment with AI help.
description:
Replit is an online coding environment: you write, run and share programs from the browser with nothing to install. It supports many languages and includes an AI assistant that can help write or explain code.

It is excellent for learning and for quickly sharing small projects. For large or sensitive projects, consider hosting and costs carefully. Free options and paid plans change, so check the official site.
use_steps: Create an account and start a new project.
Write code and press run.
Share the link or deploy.

name: Codeium (Windsurf)
tagline: AI coding assistant and editor.
best_for: Autocomplete and chat in the IDE
description:
Windsurf, from the team behind Codeium, is an AI code editor and assistant. It offers autocomplete and an agent-style chat that can read and edit files in your project.

It competes with tools like Cursor and Copilot. Features and branding have changed over time, so check the official site for the current product names, free tier and limits. As with any coding assistant, test the results and avoid pasting secrets.
use_steps: Install the editor or plugin.
Open a project and try autocomplete and chat.
Review and test generated code.

name: Google Colab
tagline: Free hosted notebooks for Python and ML.
description:
Google Colab provides free notebooks in the browser where you can run Python code, which makes it popular for data science, machine learning and teaching. Notebooks live in your Google Drive and can be shared like documents.

Free sessions have time and resource limits, and optional paid plans offer more power. It is a great way to learn without installing software. Do not upload private data you are not allowed to share.
use_steps: Open Colab with a Google account.
Create a notebook and run a code cell.
Share or save to Drive.

name: NotebookLM
tagline: Chat with your own documents and get summaries.
description:
NotebookLM from Google lets you upload your own sources, such as PDFs, notes or web pages, and then ask questions about only that material. Answers include references to the passages used, which makes checking easier.

It can also create summaries, study guides and audio overviews. It is useful for revising from your own readings, because it is less likely to wander off topic. Still compare important points with the original text. Availability and limits change, so check the official page.
use_steps: Create a notebook and add your sources.
Ask questions or request a study guide.
Check each answer against the cited passage.
cons: Only as good as your sources

name: Quizlet
tagline: Flashcards and study modes.
description:
Quizlet is a study platform built around flashcards, practice tests and games. You can create your own sets or use sets made by other learners, and the app tracks what you know.

Active recall and repetition make flashcards effective, but community sets can contain errors, so verify them with your textbook. Some modes and AI features are paid, and plans change; see the official site.
use_steps: Create a set of terms and definitions.
Study with flashcards and learn mode.
Take a practice test.

name: Anki
tagline: Spaced-repetition flashcards.
description:
Anki is a free, open-source flashcard program built around spaced repetition: cards you find hard come back sooner, and easy ones appear less often. This is one of the most evidence-supported ways to remember facts for the long term.

It takes some time to learn and the desktop interface is plain, but it is very flexible and has add-ons and shared decks. Medical and language learners use it heavily. Download from the official site; some mobile versions have different pricing.
use_steps: Install Anki and create a deck.
Add cards and study a few minutes every day.
Rate each card honestly to tune the schedule.

name: Khan Academy (Khanmigo)
tagline: Free lessons with an AI tutor option.
description:
Khan Academy offers free lessons, practice and tests across school subjects, from early maths to advanced topics. Khanmigo is its AI tutor, designed to guide students with hints and questions instead of just giving answers.

The core courses are free. Khanmigo availability and cost can vary by country and account type, so check the official site. It is a good option when you want structured learning with built-in practice.
use_steps: Create a free account and choose a course.
Watch the lesson and do the exercises.
Try the AI tutor where it is available.

name: Duolingo
tagline: Gamified language learning.
description:
Duolingo teaches languages through short, game-like lessons on your phone or browser. It tracks streaks, gives points and mixes reading, listening and speaking exercises.

It is excellent for building a daily habit and learning basic vocabulary, though most learners need extra practice such as conversation to become fluent. It has a free version with ads and paid tiers; check the official site for current features.
use_steps: Pick a language and set a daily goal.
Complete a short lesson each day.
Add real conversation practice.
cons: Ads or limits on free plan

name: Wolfram Alpha
tagline: Computational knowledge engine for maths and science.
description:
Wolfram Alpha is a computational knowledge engine. Instead of searching the web, it calculates answers: solve equations, plot functions, convert units, show chemistry data and more.

It is excellent for checking maths homework steps and for reliable factual data, because results come from curated data and computation. Step-by-step solutions are often part of the paid tier. Its input style can need practice, but it is very accurate on supported topics.
use_steps: Type an equation or question.
Read the result and the extra information.
Use step-by-step options to learn the method.
cons: Step-by-step is limited on free use
Understanding of natural language is limited

name: Elicit
tagline: AI research assistant for academic papers.
description:
Elicit helps with literature review. You ask a research question and it finds relevant academic papers, extracts key details such as methods and findings into a table and summarises them.

It can save hours at the start of a project, but you must still read the papers and check that summaries are accurate. Free and paid features change, so check the official page.
use_steps: Enter your research question.
Review the table of papers.
Open and read the important papers yourself.

name: Consensus
tagline: Search engine for scientific papers.
description:
Consensus is a search engine for scientific research. You ask a question such as whether a habit affects health, and it shows findings from peer-reviewed papers along with links.

It is a good way to find evidence quickly, but a single summary line cannot capture a study's limits. Open the papers and check study size and quality. Features and plans change; see the official site.
use_steps: Type a yes/no or research question.
Browse the listed studies.
Open the full papers for details.

name: Scholarcy
tagline: Summarises research articles into flashcards.
description:
Scholarcy turns long research papers and articles into short summary cards with key points, figures, references and limitations. It also creates flashcards.

It can speed up skimming a stack of readings, but it does not replace reading. Use it to decide what is worth a careful read. Pricing and limits change, so check the official site.
use_steps: Upload a paper or paste a link.
Read the summary card.
Read the original for details you will cite.

name: Zotero
tagline: Free reference manager.
description:
Zotero is a free, open-source reference manager. A browser button saves papers and web pages with their details, stores PDFs, and helps you create citations and bibliographies in Word and Google Docs.

It is trusted by students and researchers, supports many citation styles and works across devices. A limited amount of cloud storage is free; more is paid. Download from the official site.
use_steps: Install Zotero and the browser connector.
Save sources as you read.
Insert citations in your word processor.
cons: Takes a short time to learn

name: Semrush
tagline: SEO and marketing research suite.
description:
Semrush is an online marketing suite best known for SEO. It helps you find keywords, check which sites rank for a topic, audit a website for technical issues and study competitors.

It is powerful but expensive for hobbyists, and its data is estimated, not exact. A limited free account exists in some regions, and plans change, so check the official page. Use it to guide decisions, then confirm with your own Search Console data.
use_steps: Create an account and enter your domain or topic.
Explore keyword and competitor reports.
Compare with Search Console data.

name: Ubersuggest
tagline: Keyword ideas and basic SEO audits.
description:
Ubersuggest, from Neil Patel, offers keyword ideas, a site audit and basic backlink information. It is more affordable than big SEO suites and has a limited free option, which suits small sites and beginners.

Treat its volume and difficulty numbers as rough estimates. Pricing and limits change; check the official site.
use_steps: Enter a keyword or your domain.
Review keyword ideas and the audit.
Prioritise topics you can actually write well.

name: Google Search Console
tagline: Free tool to monitor your site in Google Search.
description:
Google Search Console is a free tool that shows how your website appears in Google Search. It reports which queries bring visitors, which pages are indexed, mobile and speed issues, and any security or manual action problems.

Every site owner should set it up. You verify ownership, submit your sitemap and then check the performance and indexing reports regularly. It gives real data from Google, which no third-party estimate can match.
use_steps: Add your site and verify ownership.
Submit your sitemap.
Check Performance and Pages reports weekly.

name: Jasper
tagline: AI writing platform for marketing teams.
description:
Jasper is an AI writing platform aimed at marketing teams. It offers templates for ads, blog posts and emails and lets you save brand voice and style guidance so that content stays consistent across a team.

It is built for business use and is mostly paid, with trials that have changed over time. Generated copy should always be fact-checked and edited by a person, especially claims about products. Compare with general assistants before paying.
use_steps: Set up your brand voice.
Choose a template and brief.
Edit and fact-check before publishing.

name: Resume Worded
tagline: Resume and LinkedIn review tool.
description:
Resume Worded reviews your resume and LinkedIn profile and gives a score with suggestions about wording, impact and formatting. It highlights weak phrases and missing results.

The free check gives a taste; deeper feedback is paid. Treat scores as hints, not truth, and keep your content honest. Pair it with feedback from a real person who knows your field. Pricing changes, so check the official site.
use_steps: Upload your resume.
Read the score and suggestions.
Rewrite weak bullets with real numbers.

name: Jobscan
tagline: Compares your resume with a job description.
description:
Jobscan compares your resume with a job description and shows which keywords and skills match or are missing. It also checks formatting issues that can confuse applicant tracking systems.

This helps you tailor each application, as long as you add only skills you truly have. A few scans are typically free and more need a subscription; check the official page. It is a guide, not a guarantee of an interview.
use_steps: Paste your resume and the job description.
Review missing keywords.
Add them only where they are true.

name: Interview Warmup (Google)
tagline: Practise interview questions with Google.
description:
Interview Warmup is a free practice tool from Google. You choose a field, see common interview questions, answer them out loud and get a transcript with insights, for example about the topics you mentioned and how long you spoke.

It is useful for building comfort speaking about yourself. It is practice, not a prediction of how a real interviewer will judge you. Combine it with your own notes and a friend's feedback.
use_steps: Open the tool and pick a role area.
Answer questions by voice.
Review the transcript and improve.
